title: Remediation SLA timers + breach alerting (with pause/override policy)
creator: Rafael Mendes
project: Reliability Program: Incident taxonomy + ownership mapping
description:
Problem
- We approved a remediation SLA matrix by severity/tier (Hosted/Dedicated/Private) and incident_type, but today we do not enforce it consistently.
- ICs often lose track of “when do we breach” for mitigation/fix targets, and escalation is ad-hoc.
- We need (1) a deterministic SLA clock, (2) a way to pause/override for force majeure/customer-caused incidents with auditability, and (3) alerting for impending breach and breach events.

Scope (this ticket)
1) Implement remediation SLA timers keyed by:
   - severity (Sev0/Sev1/Sev2/Sev3)
   - customer tier (Hosted/Dedicated/Private)
   - incident_type/subtype (from taxonomy v1)
   - “time-to-mitigate” (TTM) and “time-to-fix” (TTF) targets
2) Emit signals and alerts:
   - warning at T-30m and T-10m for Sev0/Sev1 mitigation target (TTM)
   - warning at T-60m for Sev0/Sev1 fix target (TTF) when applicable
   - breach alerts to Slack + paging rules per severity/tier
3) Document and implement pause/override policy:
   - allow pausing the SLA clock with explicit reason codes
   - require approval + audit trail
   - ensure overrides are visible in dashboards and postmortems

Non-goals
- Re-defining the SLA matrix (owned by SRE + Product via PM-912).
- Replacing postmortem RCA; this is purely timer logic + alerting + policy enforcement.
- Perfect automation for identifying customer-caused events; we will require explicit human attestation.

Proposed SLA clock rules (v1)
- Start: when incident is declared in incident-bot (timestamp incident.created_at) AND severity is set.
- If incident_type is unknown at creation time:
  - start a “classification grace period” timer (15 minutes for Sev0/Sev1; 60 minutes for Sev2/Sev3).
  - after grace, use incident_type = "unknown" (conservative/default SLA targets per tier/severity) until updated.
- Stop TTM (mitigation): when incident state transitions to "Mitigated" in incident-bot.
- Stop TTF (fix): when incident state transitions to "Resolved".
- Severity changes: recompute due times from original start time using the new severity, but record the change in an audit log. (Rationale: avoid gaming by downgrading/ upgrading late; timeline is still anchored to start.)

Pause/override policy (auditable)
- Supported pause reason codes (single-select):
  1) force_majeure_cloud_provider (e.g., region-wide cloud outage)
  2) force_majeure_internet_backbone (broad internet routing issues)
  3) customer_caused (bad client deploy, exceeded contracted load pattern, misconfiguration on Private)
  4) planned_maintenance_window (only if pre-announced and explicitly linked)
  5) other_requires_sre_approval
- Who can pause:
  - Incident Commander may request pause
  - Requires confirmation from SRE on-call (or SRE program lead delegate) for Sev0/Sev1; for Sev2/Sev3, IC can self-approve but must provide reason + link.
- Enforcement:
  - pause creates an immutable audit entry with actor, reason, timestamp, and freeform note (required)
  - total paused duration is capped at 6 hours without explicit SRE Director approval for Sev0/Sev1 (recorded as a second audit entry)
- Reporting:
  - dashboards must show: paused_duration, pause_count, and pause_reasons distribution.
  - postmortem template must include “SLA paused?” + reason.

Implementation plan
A) SLA evaluator library
- Use slo-toolkit evaluator (see PR: sources/github/slo-toolkit/pr-311-incident-sla-policy-evaluator.json).
- Config source of truth:
  - read SLA matrix (type/subtype + tier + severity => TTM/TTF) from control-plane versioned config (ENG-4825).
  - provide a safe default when taxonomy is unknown (kept deliberately strict for Hosted; aligned with Dedicated/Private commitments via PM-912).
- Provide deterministic outputs:
  - ttm_due_at, ttf_due_at
  - state: on_track | warning | breached
  - breach_type: mitigation | fix

B) Incident-bot integration
- Store SLA fields on the incident object:
  - ttm_due_at, ttf_due_at, sla_state
  - paused (bool), paused_reason, paused_total_seconds
  - audit log entries (append-only)
- Commands (Sev0–Sev3):
  - /incident sla status (prints due times, remaining time, pause state)
  - /incident sla pause --reason <code> --note <text> (with approval rules above)
  - /incident sla resume --note <text>
  - /incident sla override --ttm <duration> --ttf <duration> --reason <code> --note <text> (SRE approval required; for edge-case contracts)

C) Alerting
- Slack:
  - warnings => #incidents (threaded on incident channel if available)
  - breaches => #incidents + #eng-sre
- Paging:
  - Sev0 breach => page primary owner on-call + SRE on-call
  - Sev1 breach => page SRE on-call; notify primary owner channel
  - Sev2/S3 => Slack only
- Alert identity includes: incident_id, tier, severity, incident_type/subtype, primary_owner, ttm/ttf due times.

D) Observability + dashboards
- Emit metrics (low cardinality):
  - incidents_sla_breach_total{tier,severity,incident_type,breach_type}
  - incidents_sla_pause_total{tier,severity,pause_reason}
  - incidents_sla_warning_total{tier,severity,breach_type}
  - incidents_sla_due_seconds{tier,severity,breach_type} (gauge, sampled)
- Guardrails: incident_type is from the taxonomy allowlist only; unknown/unclassified collapses to "unknown".

Acceptance criteria
- For any new incident created in incident-bot with severity + tier:
  - SLA due times are computed and visible within 60 seconds.
  - warning messages fire at configured thresholds.
  - breach messages fire when due time is exceeded, including a link to the incident and the runbook.
- Pause/resume works and is audited:
  - cannot pause Sev0/Sev1 without SRE approval signal.
  - audit entries appear in incident timeline + exported to dashboards.
- SLA evaluation is deterministic across severity/type updates:
  - due times update predictably and are recorded.
- Dashboard can show breach rate by severity/tier/type, and excludes paused duration correctly.

Rollout
- Phase 1 (shadow): compute due times + emit metrics only (no paging), 1 week.
- Phase 2 (warn): enable Slack warnings + breaches, no paging, 1 week.
- Phase 3 (enforce): enable paging for Sev0/Sev1 breaches.
- Include a kill switch: sla_alerting_enabled and sla_paging_enabled in config.

Links
- Confluence SLA matrix: sources/confluence/eng-sre/reliability-initiatives/incident-ownership-mapping-and-remediation-sla-matrix.json
- Dashboard spec: sources/confluence/eng-platform/dashboards-and-alerts/incident-taxonomy-dashboards-spec.json
- Implementation PR (breach alerts): sources/github/redwood/pr-28635-add-remediation-sla-breaching-alert.json
- Evaluator library: sources/github/slo-toolkit/pr-311-incident-sla-policy-evaluator.json
- Incident-bot closure gating (related): sources/github/incident-bot/pr-839-enforce-postmortem-link-and-owner-before-close.json

Notes / open questions (resolved in updates below)
- What is the default SLA for incident_type="unknown"? (Resolved: conservative defaults aligned to severity/tier; see config notes in PR-28635.)
- How to handle customer-caused incidents? (Resolved: require explicit pause reason + note + SRE approval for Sev0/Sev1; audit & reporting.)
- Force majeure carve-outs? (Resolved: pause reason code + approval workflow; still track total time for transparency.)
